solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prostitute spoils the area

indicators.note: to spoil something is to damage or mess it up, so the letters of these words are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: A streetwalker is said to be ruining the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the signal to rearrange THE AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hetaera was a courtesan of ancient Greece, so the word serves as a learned synonym for a harlot.

clue.text: Man in black should be redder, we hear?

indicators.note: something we hear is spoken, so the letters are what a phrase sounds like rather than how it is written

parts.note: Titian is a reddish auburn colour named after the painter, so redder could be called more Titian

explanation.surface: A man dressed in black is told, apparently, that he ought to look more red.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian red is a reddish-gold hair colour named after the Venetian painter; MORE TITIAN, said quickly, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker traditionally wears sombre black clothes, so he is a man in black.

clue.text: Is a boy brought up to make money in Africa?

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing words up means reading them from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A question whether a youngster has been raised to earn a fortune in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ISALAD round to give the answer; in the surface it means raised as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The dalasi is the currency unit of the Gambia in West Africa.

clue.text: Worried about being bitten by 'ound, play it cool?

indicators.note: a thing bitten by teeth is held inside the mouth, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: hound as a verb means hunt; with the H dropped, as the apostrophe shows, hunt becomes 'unt

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to have cared about something is to have worried over it

explanation.surface: Someone fretting about being nipped by a dog is told to stay calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the word for worried, and 'being bitten by' sets it inside. The apostrophe in 'ound shows the dropped H: hound means hunt, said Cockney-style without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To underact is to perform with restraint, an actor's way of keeping things low-key.

clue.text: Homespun Ian, Scottish dupe led astray

indicators.note: to lead someone astray is to send them off course, so these letters are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: A simple Scotsman called Ian is conned and misled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led astray' rearranges the letters of IAN SCOTTISH DUPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun describes something plain and simple, lacking worldly refinement.

clue.text: Not green about anything — single-glazed windows being this?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: green timber is unseasoned and wet, so not green is dry
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A house with single-glazed windows is no newcomer to the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps one piece round the other. The definition is a cryptic hint: single glazing lets the wind through.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows with only one pane tend to let cold air leak in, which is what makes a room breezy.

clue.text: One restricted by narrow Anglicans?

indicators.note: something restricted by words is confined within them, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A churchman is hemmed in by narrow-minded members of the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in naRROW ANglicans. As a whole the clue points to Rowan Williams, then Archbishop of Canterbury, under pressure from conservative Anglicans.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowan Williams, as Archbishop, led the Church of England while its traditionalist wing constrained him.

clue.text: Knees-up about to start

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
to rouse game birds is to start them from cover

explanation.surface: A party is just about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' is the hunting sense: to flush game from cover. A knees-up is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouse is a bout of boisterous drinking and revelry, much like a rowdy party.

clue.text: Gym set having a game

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
a lot is a set of items, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A gymnastics group gets a match in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a Basque ball sport played against a wall.

clue.text: Film sailor, inexperienced, going the wrong way aboard ship

indicators.note: people aboard a vessel are inside it, so these letters go within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: a word going the wrong way is read backwards

parts.note: raw means inexperienced

explanation.surface: A green sailor heading off course on a ship, as in a movie plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong way' turns RAW into WAR; TAR and WAR then go 'aboard' SS.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lucas's 1977 space saga is one of the most famous movies ever made.

clue.text: City succeeded in opposition to a move

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
anti means against
a go is a move or turn in a game

explanation.surface: A city has managed to oppose a proposed relocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital of Chile, among other places so named.

clue.text: Number one in the class?

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: a genus is a class or category in biology
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The top pupil in a school form.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, one (I) goes in a biological class (GENUS); read as a whole, the brightest pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: The best pupil in a group is often a prodigy of exceptional intellect.

clue.text: Mistake with imported cut of meat being rather salty

indicators.note: something imported is brought in, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
a rack is a cut of lamb or pork ribs

explanation.surface: An error with imported ribs has left them too salty.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is British informal slang for a mistake or blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackish water is slightly briny, a mix of fresh and sea water.

clue.text: Trainee beginning to tussle with computer facility

parts.note: an interne, a variant spelling of intern, is a trainee doctor

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A new recruit starts wrestling with a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: INTERNE is a less common spelling of intern, a hospital trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide network linking computers is a facility used through them.

clue.text: Name a saint in modern setting becoming popular again

indicators.note: in places these letters within the other word
a setting surrounds something, as a mount holds a jewel

parts.note: recent means modern

explanation.surface: Naming a saint in a modern context is coming back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'setting' together signal the insertion: the modern word holds name, a and saint, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or reviving, as something returning to favour does.

clue.text: Openings beneficial to an Asian bird

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it, benefiting it
an gives A, the indefinite article
the mina, or myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Openings that suit an Asian bird, perhaps nesting holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Foramina, plural of foramen, are anatomical holes such as those in bone.

clue.text: Be prominent and big going about

indicators.note: a word going about another surrounds it

parts.note: stout means big or fat

explanation.surface: Being tall and bulky makes one conspicuous when moving around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link word but is part of the wordplay; 'going about' wraps the word for big round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be conspicuous is to catch the eye, rising above the rest.

clue.text: Army chaps providing exotic dishes

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army
chaps are males

explanation.surface: Soldiers serving up foreign food.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was Britain's Territorial Army, its volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamales are Mexican steamed parcels of maize dough, foreign fare to a British solver.

clue.text: 'Layer' carrying leaves initially, it being a bird

indicators.note: something carrying an item holds it within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a coat is a layer, as of paint

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hen that lays is carrying leaves, and turns out to be a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' in quotes invites a laying hen, but it is a coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small European songbird of the tit family.

clue.text: Available pub — marine therefore enters it

indicators.note: a thing entering goes inside, so these letters go within the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
marine relates to the sea
so means therefore

explanation.surface: A soldier at sea comes into a pub that is open.
explanation.definitionFit: Food in season is obtainable at that time of year.

clue.text: Arrest troublesome philosopher

indicators.note: troublesome letters are unruly, so they are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Police are told to take an awkward thinker into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublesome' rearranges ARREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was the French existentialist thinker.

clue.text: One old woman friend admitted to be a beast

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: someone admitted is let in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: ma is mother, the old woman
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An elderly lady lets a friend in, who turns out to be an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, so a wild animal.

clue.text: Roman art enthralling artist in French town

indicators.note: something enthralling captures and holds, so it wraps round the other letters

parts.note: ars is the Latin word for art
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Classical artwork captivates a painter in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Arras is a town in northern France, famed for its tapestries.

clue.text: General from Italy accompanying colonel in Indian city

indicators.note: in places these letters within the other word

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A senior officer from Italy travels with a colonel to India.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricola was a Roman military commander who governed Britain.

clue.text: A violent mistral? One shouldn't be afraid

indicators.note: a violent upheaval throws things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A fierce Provençal wind, yet one is told not to panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges A MISTRAL. The definition is ironic: this person panics needlessly, so is someone who ought not to be scared.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaremonger spreads needless fear, a person whose dread is unwarranted.

clue.text: Author's position not good

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a ranking is a position in a list

explanation.surface: A writer's standing is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Rankin is the Scottish crime novelist who created Inspector Rebus.

clue.text: One collects fag-ends when assistance is needed around street

parts.note: as means when

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A street cleaner picks up cigarette butts when help is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag-ends is British slang for cigarette butts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashstand is a standing receptacle for cigarette ash and butts.
